purpose: These vectors, together with the frozen layer-1 semantic specification they
apply, are the NORMATIVE specification of the assembled-map composition
algebra. Both the independent JavaScript reference implementation and the
production Rust assembler must reproduce every vector EXACTLY. Prose in AMD-008
states the thesis and the acceptance criterion; layer 1 states the semantics;
this file states the enumerated coverage of those semantics.
They are hand-derived from (a) the source-map v3 wire format as implemented by
the accepted decoder, and (b) the real CodeTransform chunk-emission semantics.
They were NOT generated by either implementation, and no vector's expected
output was copied from a program's output.
knownGaps: Expected outputs are a PARTIAL projection (code + segments) rather than the complete MapArtifact the amendment compares; completing them is required before freeze.

coordinateConventions.columns: 0-based UTF-16 CODE UNITS, as on the wire and as measured by String.prototype.length
warning: A UTF-16 code-unit column is not a Unicode code-point index and not a UTF-8
byte offset. Vector V5 pins all three apart deliberately: for the same
position they are 11, 10, and 13 respectively. An implementation that counts
code points (the natural error in Python-like languages) or bytes (the
natural error in Rust) fails V5 and only V5.

overwriteNonEmpty: a non-empty overwrite pushes exactly ONE token at the replacement's generated
start, mapped to the OVERWRITTEN RANGE'S ORIGINAL START. There is no
character-level correspondence inside the replacement, so no interior tokens.
overwriteEmpty: Same arm: `if content.is_empty() { continue; }` — an empty overwrite (the
export removal) emits NO token and advances no generated position.
followingChunkTransition: emit_mapped_content: every Original chunk unconditionally pushes a token at its
OWN start before scanning interior boundaries. An overwrite (empty or not) that
is followed by surviving text is therefore always followed by a token at the
old end. A TERMINAL overwrite has no following Original chunk and so has no
such token. V1 pins the terminal case; V2 pins the non-terminal case.
interiorLineStarts: emit_mapped_content emits interior tokens at newline boundaries, but filters
`position + 1 < content_len` — so a newline that ENDS a chunk emits no extra
token. V1 and V2 both rely on this: the trailing newline of a chunk is silent.
lookupIsLineScoped: the applicable segment is the last one ON THAT GENERATED LINE at or before the
column. A line with no earlier segment is UNMAPPED — the lookup does not fall
through to a previous line. V2 pins this: the transition token lands on a line
whose only segment is to its right, so the transition is SOURCELESS.
wireOrderIsObservable: a zero generated-column delta pushes an ADDITIONAL segment rather than
replacing one, so several segments may share one coordinate and their wire
order is preserved. Combined with resolveAt taking the LAST applicable, that
order is semantically observable. V3 pins it.

vectors.intent: Rename pass token geometry, and a TERMINAL removal which therefore has no following-chunk token.
derivation: oldGen text is 43 units: line 0 'const __sfc__ = {}' (18), line 1
'export default __sfc__;' (23). The rename occurrences are at oldGen (0,6)
and (1,15); '__sfc__' is 7 units and '_sfc_main' is 9, a +2 delta.
PASS 1 chunks: Original[0,6) | Overwritten@6 | Original[13,34) |
Overwritten@34 | Original[41,43). The split happens only at EDIT boundaries,
so [13,34) is one chunk spanning the newline; its interior line-start token
is emitted while scanning that chunk, not by a separate chunk.
- (0,0) survives, unshifted.
- the input segment at (0,6) is INSIDE the overwrite, so it is dropped and
replaced by the single overwrite token at newGen (0,6) whose original is
the last applicable input at the overwritten range's original start
- the following Original chunk starts at oldGen (0,13); after a 9-unit
replacement the generated column is 6+9=15, so a token is emitted at
newGen (0,15). Line-scoped lookup at oldGen (0,13) finds (0,6) as the
last applicable on line 0 -> authored (1,6).
- line 1 repeats the pattern: (1,0) survives; the overwrite token lands at
(1,15) -> authored (2,15); the following chunk token lands at newGen
PASS 2 removes 'export default _sfc_main;\n' from the pass-1 text. In pass-1
coordinates that text is 47 units and the target occupies [21,47) — it ends
exactly at end of text, so the removal is TERMINAL: there is no following
Original chunk and therefore NO transition token. Every pass-1 token on line
1 is inside the removed range and is dropped. Line 0 is untouched.

vectors.intent: A NON-TERMINAL removal does have a following-chunk token, and that token is SOURCELESS when its line has no applicable segment at or before it.
derivation: Pass 1 behaves exactly as in V1 for lines 0 and 1; line 2 has no rename
occurrence, so its single segment survives unshifted at (2,6).
Pass 2: the pass-1 text is line 0 'const _sfc_main = {}' (20), line 1
'export default _sfc_main;' (25), line 2 'const tail = 1' (14), each newline
terminated: 62 units. The removal target occupies [21,47), and text continues
to 62, so a following Original chunk [47,62) EXISTS. That chunk emits a token
at its own start: generated position after the removal is (1,0), and its
original position is the lookup of pass-1 coordinate (2,0).
Line-scoped lookup at (2,0): the only segment on line 2 is at column 6, which
is AFTER column 0, so there is no applicable segment on that line. The lookup
does not fall back to line 1. The emitted token is therefore SOURCELESS.
This is the vector that fails an implementation which (a) omits the
following-chunk token entirely, or (b) performs a global rather than
line-scoped last-applicable lookup and wrongly inherits authored (2,15).
The surviving line-2 segment shifts from line 2 to line 1, keeping column 6.

vectors.intent: Two segments sharing one generated coordinate keep their wire order. A multiset or column-sorted comparator cannot distinguish this vector from its swap.
derivation: No rename or removal occurrence appears in this fragment, so both passes are
identity and every segment survives unshifted, IN ORDER.
Both segments occupy generated (0,0). The decoder emits them in wire order
because the second carries a zero column delta, and resolveAt selects the
LAST applicable — so a consumer at (0,0) resolves authored (5,5), not (1,0).
Swapping the two changes that answer while leaving every multiset, every
per-line bag, and every column-sorted list identical. The expected sequence
below is therefore order-significant and is the discriminating case for
positional comparison.

vectors.provisionalLayer1Policy: This vector's derivation decides a LAYER-1 chaining/table-policy question (stable-append-no-dedup for sources/names) rather than merely applying an already-frozen one, which the artifact's own status/purpose fields forbid until layer 1 is frozen. It is retained as a proposed policy statement and coverage sketch ONLY — not authoritative test content — pending independent layer-1 freeze; the frozen layer-1 specification governs if it settles this question differently, and this vector must be re-derived (or confirmed unchanged) against layer 1 once it exists, not treated as already-normative.
vectors.intent: Source and name tables are a STABLE APPEND with no deduplication, even when both fragments declare identical spellings; template indices are remapped by the append offset.

placement.templateStartLineDerivation: the script code ends with a newline so the write cursor is at line 1; the assembler then unconditionally writes one separator newline before the template code, putting the template at line 2. Placement is DERIVED from the write grammar here, not supplied as an independent input.

derivation: Both fragments name the same authored file and the same authored symbol. A
deduplicating merge would emit sources ['Comp.vue'] and names ['count'] and
leave both fragments' indices at 0 — which is why deduplication is forbidden:
it destroys the one-to-one (origin, local_index) provenance that makes each
output row attributable to exactly one fragment.
Under stable append, script rows come first in their original order, then
template rows in theirs: sources ['Comp.vue','Comp.vue'], names
['count','count']. Script indices are unchanged (offset 0); template indices
shift by the script table lengths (offset 1).
The script rename moves nothing here: the occurrence is at (0,6) and the
single segment is exactly at the overwrite start, so it is dropped and
replaced by the overwrite token at the same coordinate with the same original
position and NAME — a rewrite never drops or renames a name binding. The
following Original chunk emits its token at newGen (0,15) via line-scoped
lookup at oldGen (0,13), which resolves to the (0,6) segment, carrying its
name index as well.
The template fragment is not rewritten, so its segment shifts by placement
only. The script code ends with a newline, leaving the cursor at line 1, and
the assembler then writes one separator newline before the template code — so
the template begins at line 2 and its (0,9) segment lands at (2,9). Reading
the separator as absent, and placing the template at line 1, is the natural
off-by-one this vector exists to catch.

vectors.intent: Columns are UTF-16 code units — not code points, and not UTF-8 bytes. This vector separates all three.
derivation: The line is 'const ' (6 units) + U+1D400 MATHEMATICAL BOLD CAPITAL A (a
surrogate PAIR, 2 UTF-16 units) + ' = ' (3 units) + '__sfc__' (7 units).
The '__sfc__' occurrence therefore begins at:
UTF-16 code-unit column 11   <- the wire-correct value used below
Unicode code-point index 10  <- what a code-point-counting language reports
UTF-8 byte offset 13         <- what a byte-counting language reports
All three were verified directly against the real string. An implementation
that conflates any two of them fails this vector and no other.
After the rename the replacement is 9 units, so the following Original chunk
token lands at column 11+9 = 20, and its line-scoped lookup at old column 18
(11 + 7, the overwritten range's end) resolves to the (0,11) segment.
The removal pass finds no occurrence and is identity.

vectors.intent: A CR retained before a LF occupies a real column; lines split on LF only.
derivation: The accepted line table splits on LF and RETAINS the CR, so line 0 is
'const a = 1\r' — 12 units, the CR occupying column 11. Stripping the CR
would under-count every line by one and shift every subsequent column.
Line 1 is 'const __sfc__ = {}\r'. The rename occurrence is at column 6, the
replacement is 9 units, so the following Original chunk token lands at column
6+9 = 15, resolving through line-scoped lookup at old column 13 to the (1,6)
segment. The CR is inside that following chunk and needs no token of its own.
The removal pass finds no occurrence: the target ends with LF, and no
'export default _sfc_main;\n' appears here.

vectors.intent: A sourceless segment acts as a barrier: a lookup landing at or after it yields a sourceless result rather than inheriting the previous source-bearing segment.
derivation: The sourceless input segment sits at column 3, BEFORE the rename occurrence
at [6,13). It is outside the overwritten range, so it survives, and being
before the edit it is unshifted.
The overwrite token's original position comes from the line-scoped
last-applicable lookup at old column 6. The candidates on line 0 at or before
column 6 are (0,0) source-bearing and (0,3) SOURCELESS; the last is the
sourceless one, so the overwrite token is SOURCELESS.
The following Original chunk starts at old column 13; the same lookup again
yields the (0,3) sourceless segment, so that token is SOURCELESS too. It
lands at new column 6+9 = 15.
This is the vector that fails an implementation which treats a sourceless
segment as transparent — skipping past it to find the nearest source-bearing
segment. Such an implementation reports authored (1,0) at both positions and
so fabricates provenance for text the fragment deliberately left unmapped.
The barrier is exercised at two independent lookups, and no two emitted
segments share a coordinate, so this vector does not depend on any rule about
coincident tokens.

failClosedVectors.intent: Malformed source-map JSON is UncomposableInputMap, never a degraded success.
A non-3 version is rejected before any composition.
An absent `mappings` member is NOT silently read as an empty map.

An out-of-range VLQ quantity is rejected rather than silently wrapping to zero. The accepted decoder is lenient here: 'A' and 'ggggggE' both decode to a sourceless segment at (0,0) because a 32-bit shift wraps. Only 'A' is a conforming encoding.

A source index with no corresponding table row is rejected. The mappings string must be a WELL-FORMED 4-field segment so that this vector exercises index bounds and not segment arity: 'AC' decodes to two fields and is rejected earlier as a malformed segment, which is a different category. 'ACAA' decodes to generated-column delta 0, source delta +1, original line delta 0, original column delta 0 — i.e. source index 1 against a one-row table.
An indexed (`sections`) map is not a flat map and is rejected; a conforming consumer would prefer `sections` over `mappings`.

A template-only cell whose compiler produced a SYNTHETIC empty script map is NOT a missing required map. Map-requiredness comes from the authored-fragment inventory, not from the presence of a compiled script block.

expected.note: synthetic sourceless script contributes no segments and no table rows; composition proceeds
